report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is *plausible and supported by small human studies*, but it is not universally true. The likely benefit is not the open window or door itself; it is improved bedroom ventilation and lower accumulation of exhaled CO₂ and other indoor pollutants.

A controlled crossover field study found that lowering bedroom CO₂ improved objectively measured sleep quality, perceived air freshness, next-day sleepiness, concentration, and logical-thinking performance. [https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26452168/](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26452168/) A later field-intervention study specifically examined opening bedroom windows and doors, reporting evidence that sufficient pollutant dilution/removal supports better bedroom air quality, sleep, and next-day cognition. [https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/a-field-intervention-study-of-the-effects-of-window-and-door-open](https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/a-field-intervention-study-of-the-effects-of-window-and-door-open)

Important limitations: the evidence base is still relatively limited, many outcomes are self-reported, and an open window/door may not provide adequate airflow in every building or weather condition. Benefits can be offset by cold/heat, outdoor pollution, pollen (especially for allergic rhinitis), or noise. Allergic rhinitis itself is associated with poorer subjective and objectively measured sleep, so admitting pollen could reasonably worsen sleep for susceptible people. [https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0228533](https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0228533) Outdoor noise is also an established cause of sleep disturbance. [https://www.who.int/tools/compendium-on-health-and-environment/environmental-noise/](https://www.who.int/tools/compendium-on-health-and-environment/environmental-noise/)

**Practical takeaway:** Try an ajar door or window if outdoor air is quiet, clean, secure, and temperature-comfortable; otherwise, mechanical ventilation may deliver the same underlying benefit without those trade-offs.
